name: Dalmia Bharat Ltd
title: Dalmia Bharat Ltd - 542216 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Dalmia Bharat (cement) posted record Q4 EBITDA of Rs 902 crore and FY26 EBITDA Rs 3,083 crore, but West Asia cost shock of Rs 125-150/ton hits Q1 and FY27 capex is Rs 3,200-3,400 crore with no new capacity announced.

summary.headline: Dalmia Bharat Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 14% YoY to INR902 crore, with FY26 EBITDA a record INR3,083 crore and PAT INR1,157 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 volume grew 3% YoY to 8.8 million tons, held back by an unplanned kiln breakdown in East India in March (about 1.5 lakh tons of clinker and 3 lakh tons of cement lost). EBITDA rose to INR902 crore, up 14% YoY and 50% QoQ, with EBITDA per ton of INR1,023. Management said Q4 cost per ton was the lowest quarterly level in five years, but flagged a West Asia-driven cost increase of INR125-150 per ton expected in Q1 FY27, which it said it has begun passing on through April price hikes. Net debt was INR1,428 crore (0.46x net debt/EBITDA).

financial_highlights.change: +INR260/t QoQ adjusted for INR46 crore one-off incentive in Q3

financial_highlights.metric: Raw material cost per ton of production

financial_highlights.change: Down INR183/t from INR3,973 in Q1 FY25
Q4 accrual INR45 crore, collections only INR14 crore

segments.name: Cement (India, consolidated)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 8.8 Mt (+3% YoY) after March breakdown; realisations flattish YoY but up about 1.7% QoQ adjusting for INR46 crore one-off incentive in Q3. Fourth-largest cement player with about 50 Mtpa capacity across 23+ states.

segments.name: Renewables / power
segments.commentary: Added about 180 MW RE capacity in FY26; 128 MW more to be commissioned soon, taking RE capacity to 576 MW.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 cost increase expected at INR125-150/t vs Q4 FY26: packing INR80-90/t, balance split between logistics and power and fuel.
Management said April price increases have so far passed through cost increases; expects to protect margins, though it is dynamic.
Internal target of INR50-100/t annual cost take-out; Q4-on-Q4 adjusted reduction of INR125-130/t cited.
Capacity of 61.5 Mtpa expected in 18-20 months from Belgaum, Pune and Kadapa; Kadapa commissioning now Q2-Q3 FY28; Belgaum slightly ahead of schedule.
Target 72-75 Mtpa by FY28 (8-9 quarters); long-term 110-130 Mtpa milestone unchanged.
FY27 total capex INR3,200-3,400 crore, of which about INR2,200-2,300 crore expansion; balance roughly INR1,000 crore regular/maintenance capex.
Aim to grow volume better than industry in FY27; industry demand CAGR of 7-8% expected medium term.
Incentive booking for FY27 expected around INR200 crore.
capex_capacity: Capacity 50 Mtpa currently; Belgaum, Pune and Kadapa projects take it to 61.5 Mtpa in 18-20 months.
Belgaum civil work complete, E&I work started; commissioning expected a little ahead of schedule. Kadapa key equipment ordered; minor Q4 delays, now expected Q2-Q3 FY28.
Project capex outflow about INR3,200 crore over the last two fiscal years; FY27 expansion cash outflow about INR2,200 crore.
Pune GU and Chennai bulk terminal progressing satisfactorily.
Management declined to give clinker utilisation (overall or regional) or split of capex beyond the broad guidance; industry utilisation estimated at 65-70%.
demand_pricing: Management expects cement demand CAGR of 7-8% medium term; April demand described as holding up, but too early to call a slowdown; H2 FY27 seen as the real test.
Price increases in April across most key markets; management says cost increases have been passed through, with recovery above cost impact targeted; no quantification given.
Packing cost pressure from bag supply crunch and PP granule prices; petcoke about $160/t; Rupee depreciation adding to costs.
Freight sensitivity: each 5% rise in diesel price adds about INR15/t to freight cost.
Trade share 67%, premium share 24% in Q4; premiumisation push continues in FY27 with new premium product Weather 365.
CC ratio fell from about 1.7 to 1.6 over roughly three years; management targets improvement over 3-5 years.
Blended cement ratio improved to 83% in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Volume outlook and market share given continued share loss?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prioritises profitable volume; Q4 hit by East India breakdown; Q3 volume grew 10%; aim to outperform industry in coming quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Q1 cost inflation breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 impact INR125-150/t vs Q4, of which packing INR80-90/t; rest logistics and power and fuel; mitigation via fuel mix and logistics.

qa_highlights.question: Total capex for FY27 and split?
qa_highlights.answer: INR3,200-3,400 crore total, about INR2,200-2,300 crore for expansion projects; remaining roughly INR1,000 crore for regular operations, not split further.

qa_highlights.question: Reconciliation of fixed asset addition (~INR3,500 crore) vs capex outflow (~INR2,000 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Significant CWIP remains in other financial liabilities as payable; cash outflow deferred due to geopolitical situation, to be paid over next few quarters; FY27 number includes liabilities carried from FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 75 Mtpa target still by FY28 given Kadapa delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says it is still chasing 72-75 Mtpa in 8-9 quarters; slips of a quarter or a few million tons possible; new announcements to follow, no details given.

qa_highlights.question: Stake sale in IEX?
qa_highlights.answer: IEX is non-core; half the position already liquidated; balance to be sold at the right time.

qa_highlights.question: Industry capacity addition and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry adding 160-170 Mt over FY26-28, about 40 Mt commissioned in FY26 so far; utilisation 65-70%, expected similar in FY27.

risks_watch: Cost pressure from petcoke, packing and diesel: Q1 FY27 headwind INR125-150/t; sustainability of April price hikes is unproven.
Incentive receivables: INR839 crore outstanding at year-end with only INR14 crore collected in Q4 due to state government payment delays.
Execution risk on Kadapa (now Q2-Q3 FY28) and on announcing new capacity to reach 75 Mtpa; no details yet on new projects.
Demand: management says any slowdown may take a couple of quarters to show; H2 FY27 is the test.
Volume: 2% FY26 growth, persistent market share loss questions; East India kiln breakdown impact.
Balance-sheet deferred capex payables could lift FY27 cash outflow; contingent liabilities at 6% of equity.

Management declined to answer on grinding capacity size in the Northeast, mineral reserve additions from Tamil Nadu preferred-bidder wins, and the SFIO mutual fund case (company said it has received no communication).
summary.management_tone: Confident on cost leadership, balance sheet and pricing recovery, but guarded on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to quantify price hikes, capex breakdown, capacity sizing and fuel mix, citing a dynamic environment.
key_quotes: In this quarter, we delivered the lowest quarterly total cost per ton in the last five years, which demonstrates our unwavering commitment to be one of the lowest-cost producers.
As of now, I think, the impact of cost has been passed on.
We lost somewhere of roughly 1.5 lakh tons of clinker and 300,000 (tons) of cement, and that is the reason that, you see subdued growth in quarter 4.
I think it's too early to decide whether there's a slowdown or not in April.

adds.what: Belgaum, Pune and Kadapa projects taking capacity to 61.5 Mtpa (from 50 Mtpa)
128 MW renewable energy capacity taking RE to 576 MW

growth.why: Management targets 72-75 Mtpa by FY28 with 61.5 Mtpa in 18-20 months from Belgaum, Pune and Kadapa (Kadapa slipping to Q2-Q3 FY28) and FY27 expansion capex of INR2,200 crore, but no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given and April price hikes are unquantified.
